governance_policy.policy_name: Advanced Analytica Grammar and Punctuation Standard
governance_policy.approval_signoff: Pending Advanced Analytica brand review for policy version 1.0.0.
governance_policy.policy_summary: Sets practical house conventions for clear, consistent British English in support of Creative, Assured and Practical writing. Intentional fragments are welcome when they sharpen meaning. Grammar choices should help readers understand the message.

companion_policies.relationship: Defines the three tone principles and owns the shared semantic rules referenced here.

scope.applies_to: Authored Advanced Analytica prose, headings, lists and labels across websites, proposals, reports, presentations and internal communications.
exclusions: Faithful quotations and required legal or source wording retain their original form.
Code, identifiers, URLs and machine-readable data keep the syntax their function requires.
Labelled examples of wording to revise are excluded from whole-document style counts.
precedence: Preserve accuracy, meaning, official names and required legal or source wording.
Apply a recorded client or publication convention to the specified deliverable.
Apply each canonical rule in this standard or the TOV policy within its stated scope.
Use editorial judgement for contextual suggestions and record exceptions where needed.
scope.exceptions: Do not turn a house preference into a claim that all other usage is grammatically incorrect. Deliberate fragments and justified stylistic choices can pass when they improve understanding.

principle_alignment.guidance: Allow purposeful fragments, rhythm and expressive headings while keeping meaning clear.
Use precise punctuation, accurate figures, faithful quotations and consistent terminology.
Make instructions, lists, dates, units and references easy to understand and use.

requirements: Use British English house spellings: organise, analyse, organisation, colour and centre.
Use licence and practice as nouns; use license and practise as verbs. Use programme for general initiatives and program for software.
Keep spelling consistent within authored prose. Preserve official names, faithful quotations, code and exact source text.
exceptions: A specified client locale can override the spelling default for that deliverable; record it and apply it consistently.

examples.pass: We analyse how the programme works.
examples.revise: We analyze how the program works.
examples.reason: Use the house spellings for a general business initiative.

rules.machine_check: Use a British English dictionary to flag possible inconsistencies. Check word meaning and scope before confirming a failure. Do not replace text inside names, quotations, URLs, identifiers or code.

requirements: Use sentence case for headings: capitalise the first word, proper names and established acronyms.
Omit the final full stop in a heading. Keep internal full stops when a heading contains two short statements. Use a question mark for a real question.
Purposeful fragments are allowed. Make the heading informative and let the following text add useful detail.
exceptions: Preserve the official capitalisation of product names, document titles being cited and exact interface labels.

examples.pass: A clear scope. A tested build
examples.revise: A Clear Scope. A Tested Build.
examples.reason: Use sentence case and omit the final full stop.

rules.machine_check: Assess rendered heading text rather than Markdown markers. Check case in context; preserve proper names, acronyms and exact interface labels. Flag a terminal full stop for revision; retain meaningful internal punctuation.

requirements: Use complete sentences where the reader needs a full explanation. Keep subjects, verbs and references easy to follow.
Intentional fragments are welcome when they sharpen meaning, establish rhythm or label a clear action. Use them purposefully in headlines, short copy and lists.
Avoid accidental fragments, comma splices and strings of short statements that obscure the relationship between ideas.
Follow the shared TOV guidance on active voice and sentence length.

examples.pass: A clear scope. A tested build. A team ready to use it.
examples.revise: Because the workflow. Which the team.
examples.reason: Purposeful fragments communicate an idea; incomplete clauses here obscure it.

rules.machine_check: Assess meaning and context before flagging a fragment. Do not fail text solely because it lacks a finite verb. Treat uncertain grammar suggestions as REVIEW. Resolve shared rules from their source instead of inventing new length or active-voice thresholds.

requirements: Use commas to separate list items, introductory material and non-essential clauses when they help the reader follow the sentence.
Omit the serial comma in a simple list. Add it before the final and or or when it removes ambiguity or separates complex items.
Do not join two complete sentences with a comma alone. Use a full stop, a suitable conjunction or a semicolon.
exceptions: A client or publication can require a consistent serial-comma convention; record that override.

examples.pass: The scope is clear. The owner is missing.
examples.revise: The scope is clear, the owner is missing.

rules.machine_check: Review clause structure and list meaning in context. A serial comma is allowed when it improves clarity; its presence is not an automatic failure. Flag comma splices with an excerpt and suggested correction.

requirements: Use a colon after a clear lead-in to introduce an explanation, example or list.
Use a semicolon to connect closely related complete sentences or separate complex list items. Prefer a full stop when that is easier to read.
Do not use repeated colons or semicolons to carry a sentence through several changes of thought.

examples.pass: Check three things: scope, ownership and access.
examples.revise: The things to check are: scope, ownership and access.
examples.reason: Make the lead-in complete rather than separating the verb from its list.

rules.machine_check: Check punctuation against clause structure and reader understanding. Semicolons are permitted. Technical syntax and exact interface text are out of scope.

requirements: Use an apostrophe plus s for singular possession, including singular names ending in s. Use an apostrophe after s for regular plural possession.
Use its for possession and it's for it is or it has. Form ordinary plurals without apostrophes.
Use a curly apostrophe in polished prose where supported. A straight apostrophe is acceptable in plain text and technical formats.

examples.reason: This example refers to one client, so the possessive needs an apostrophe.

rules.machine_check: Assess whether the writer means singular possession, plural possession or an ordinary plural before suggesting a correction. Do not fail straight apostrophes in technical or plain-text contexts.

requirements: Use double quotation marks for direct quotations and single quotation marks for a quotation within a quotation or a term being discussed.
Use curly quotation marks in polished publication copy where supported; straight marks are acceptable in plain text and technical formats.
Place punctuation inside the closing mark when it belongs to the quoted material; otherwise place it outside. Preserve the quoted wording and meaning.
Identify omissions or editorial additions transparently. Apply the canonical source-attribution and evidence requirements in the TOV policy.
exceptions: A required publication style can override quotation-mark typography; preserve quotation accuracy.

examples.pass: She described the process as “ready for review”.
examples.revise: She described the process as “ready for review.”
examples.reason: The full stop belongs to the surrounding sentence rather than the quoted phrase.

rules.machine_check: Review quotation boundaries, punctuation ownership and fidelity against the supplied source. Do not alter code strings or exact source text to enforce typography. Return REVIEW if the source needed to verify a quotation is unavailable.

requirements: Prefer a full stop, comma or colon when it expresses the relationship clearly. Use a spaced en dash for an occasional aside in prose.
Use hyphens where they clarify a compound modifier before a noun. Do not add a hyphen after an adverb ending in ly.
Write ranges with to in ordinary prose. An unspaced en dash is acceptable in compact tables and charts.
Avoid unnecessary compound labels. Use familiar terms and preserve the spelling of established technical names.

examples.pass: The agent uses real-time data and updates the record in real time.
examples.revise: The agent uses real time data and updates the record in real-time.
examples.reason: The compound modifier before data takes a hyphen; the adverbial phrase does not.

rules.machine_check: Check the function of each dash or hyphen and whether it helps understanding. Flag repeated dash interruptions for REVIEW. Do not treat a minus sign, identifier, URL or code operator as prose punctuation.

requirements: Use punctuation to make the point clear and measured. Exclamation marks are not used in authored brand prose.
Use a question mark for a genuine question. Questions and expressive devices are optional; give the reader a useful reason to engage.
exceptions: Exclude faithful quotations, required source wording, code, exact interface labels, URLs and Markdown image syntax.
Labelled examples of wording to revise are excluded from whole-document style counts. Evaluate them separately only when requested.

examples.reason: Ask a useful question and keep emphasis measured.

rules.machine_check: Count exclamation marks only after scope exclusions. Target = 0 in eligible authored brand prose; a count above zero is a style violation. Question marks do not establish engagement on their own.

requirements: Use bullets for parallel items and numbers when order matters. Keep the grammatical form consistent within a list.
Start each bullet with a capital letter unless it begins with an identifier whose case must be preserved.
End complete sentences with full stops. Omit final full stops from short labels and fragments. Avoid mixing forms within one list.
Use a clear lead-in and avoid trailing commas or semicolons on ordinary bullet items.
exceptions: Preserve exact code, mathematical notation, quoted lists and structured data.

examples.pass:
1. Agree the scope.
2. Name the owner.
examples.revise:
1. Agree the scope,
2. Naming the owner;
examples.reason: Keep the steps parallel and punctuate complete instructions with full stops.

rules.machine_check: Inspect rendered list structure and grammatical parallelism. Distinguish sentence bullets from fragments. List punctuation suggestions requiring interpretation are REVIEW, not unconditional failure.

requirements: In ordinary prose, spell out one to nine and use numerals for 10 and above. Use numerals for measurements, percentages, dates, comparisons and technical data.
Use a decimal point and grouping commas for values of 1,000 or more in reader-facing prose. Keep machine-readable data and identifiers in their required format.
Preserve source values and meaningful precision. If rounding is useful, use the stated method or round to the nearest chosen precision and label the result as approximate.
Do not round selectively to strengthen a claim. Do not round values used to decide whether a threshold has been met. Retain the required precision for that decision.
exceptions: A required reporting method, scientific convention or client data format takes precedence over the prose default.

examples.pass: Illustrative value: 64.6%. Rounded to the nearest whole percentage: approximately 65%.
examples.revise: Illustrative value: 64.6%. Rounded to the nearest whole percentage: 64%.
examples.reason: Use consistent rounding and make the approximation explicit.

rules.machine_check: Compare reported values with supplied sources and declared precision. Use decimal arithmetic for rounding checks. Flag missing sources or a material precision change for REVIEW. Check technical contexts before flagging a numeral below 10.

requirements: Write human-readable dates as 11 November 2026, with no ordinal suffix or comma. Short month names are acceptable in compact tables.
Use the 24-hour clock for schedules, such as 14:30. Include a time zone when readers could interpret the time differently.
For UK schedules, use Europe/London to determine the correct GMT or BST designation for the stated date. Use explicit dates when relative wording could become unclear.
Write periods unambiguously, such as every two weeks or twice a month. Use ISO dates and timestamps in machine-readable metadata.
exceptions: A specified client locale may use another unambiguous format. Preserve exact source quotations and machine formats.

examples.reason: State an unambiguous date, time and relevant zone.

rules.machine_check: Detect ambiguous numeric dates and conflicting time notation for REVIEW. Verify stated dates, times and zones using supplied context and a time-zone-aware date library. Do not apply prose formatting to ISO metadata.

requirements: Use the appropriate currency symbol, such as £1,200. In mixed-currency or international contexts, make the currency explicit, such as GBP 1,200.
Use numerals with % and no intervening space. Use a space between a number and a unit, such as 250 ms or 5 kg, unless the unit convention specifies otherwise.
Preserve unit symbols and case. Distinguish bits from bytes and decimal units such as GB from binary units such as GiB.
State a comparison baseline and distinguish a percentage change from a change in percentage points when the distinction matters.

examples.pass: Illustration: a rise from 20% to 25% is 5 percentage points.
examples.revise: Illustration: a rise from 20% to 25% is 5%.
examples.reason: Distinguish the change in percentage points from the relative percentage change.

rules.machine_check: Check symbols, units, scale and comparison meaning against the supplied values. Flag missing or conflicting units for REVIEW. Avoid global replacements inside technical expressions.

requirements: Explain an unfamiliar abbreviation on first relevant use, then use it consistently. Familiar terms such as AI can stand alone when the audience understands them.
Use an approved product or service name exactly. Confirm an unfamiliar brand acronym or expansion against supplied approved terminology before using it.
Avoid inventing acronyms, repeating unnecessary expansions or substituting jargon for a useful explanation.

examples.pass: The application programming interface (API) connects the order system.
examples.revise: The API leverages an iPaaS across the RAG ecosystem.
examples.reason: Explain unfamiliar terms for a general business audience.

rules.machine_check: Evaluate familiarity against the audience and supplied terminology. Return REVIEW when an official name or expansion cannot be verified. Do not guess expansions or require every familiar acronym to be written out.

requirements: Write Advanced Analytica with its approved capitalisation. Use we, you and your naturally where they help; third-person company descriptions are permitted.
Use singular agreement for the company and for a team considered as one unit. Make pronoun references clear and use respectful, inclusive wording; singular they is acceptable.
Use lowercase for generic job descriptions. Preserve the official capitalisation of a formal title used with a name or in a role listing.
Use I for a subject, me for an object and myself only when the sentence calls for a reflexive or emphatic form.
exceptions: Preserve official names and faithful quotations, including their original spelling and grammar.

examples.pass: Advanced Analytica works with your team.
examples.revise: Advanced Analytica work with your team.
examples.reason: Use singular agreement for the company.

rules.machine_check: Assess names, agreement and pronoun reference in context. Respect a person's stated name, title and pronouns. Do not fail text because it uses third person or singular they.

requirements: Use bold sparingly for a key point, label or action. Keep ordinary prose in sentence case and use capitals for official names and established acronyms.
Reserve underlining for the presentation of links. Use italics sparingly for light emphasis or cited titles.
Use one space between sentences. Do not add spaces before commas, full stops, colons or semicolons in English prose.
Preserve indentation, alignment and spacing required by code, tables and structured data.

examples.pass: Agree the scope. Then name the owner.
examples.revise: Agree the scope.  Then name the owner.
examples.reason: Use one space between prose sentences.

rules.machine_check: Check spacing only in eligible prose after parsing markup. Treat formatting density as contextual REVIEW. Do not rewrite code indentation, table syntax, line breaks or exact technical strings.

requirements: Use descriptive link text that tells the reader what they will open. Keep the complete working destination in the link target.
Give the reader enough source information to identify the evidence behind a material claim. Follow the canonical evidence and attribution rule in the TOV policy.
Use a short visible web address only when the address itself is useful, such as a contact detail. Preserve complete URLs where the medium requires them.
Do not silently rewrite quoted wording, titles or numbers to match the house style.
exceptions: Exact URLs can be necessary in technical instructions, references, plain-text output and audit records.

examples.reason: The label identifies the destination. The example.com URL is illustrative.

rules.machine_check: Review link labels and destination structure in context. Verify a destination when access is available; do not claim that a link is live from syntax alone. Flag an unavailable source needed to check a claim for REVIEW.

shared_rule_references.topic: Plain language, optional contractions and sentence-length guidance

governance_policy.reference_resolution: Load both local policy files once and index them by element_id and rule_id. A source_reference identifies the canonical definition of a delegated requirement or metric. Apply each canonical rule once per finding; do not recursively expand companion links or count the same issue twice. A missing or mismatched reference is REVIEW and must be resolved before claiming a complete check.

assessment.requirements: Record the rule, scope, excerpt and reason for each finding. Treat uncertain interpretation or unavailable context as REVIEW. Use NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason for excluded content. Automated semantic results are recommendations; an editor confirms the outcome.
assessment.deterministic_checks: Use deterministic checks only after excluding code, exact source text, markup syntax and other protected spans. Keyword matches and parser guesses are review signals unless a scoped rule defines a clear violation.
assessment.limitations: This file specifies evaluation requirements; it does not implement a complete grammar checker. Structural validation and generated-guide checks do not establish that arbitrary copy complies with every semantic rule.
assessment.approval: Use the approval roles and workflow in governance_policy.json. Editing a draft does not record policy approval. Record the approval and effective date before activating this standard.

machine_evaluable_fields.evaluation: Count ! in eligible authored brand prose after all scope exclusions. Target = 0. A count above zero is a style violation; excluded example failures, image syntax, code and quoted text do not contribute.

Count clear extra spaces between prose sentences or spaces before commas, full stops, colons and semicolons after scope parsing. Flag uncertain boundaries for REVIEW. Do not inspect code or table alignment as prose.

Semantic recommendation with excerpt and reason. Assess sentence case and terminal punctuation in rendered headings, preserving names and acronyms. Internal full stops, meaningful questions and intentional fragments are allowed.

reference_material.title: PwC grammar and punctuation guide
reference_material.usage: Consulted as a topic checklist. Advanced Analytica house choices and examples are authored for this standard. PwC-specific naming, approvals and network conventions are not adopted.

policy_metadata.snapshot_maintenance: Refresh this packaged reference from its authoring project; operative rules are unchanged.
